Ablaut – A phenomenon in which the vowels in a word change depending on its form or usage, often seen in verb conjugations.

Accent – The emphasis or stress placed on certain syllables in speech, which can also refer to regional or social varieties of a language.

Affix – A morpheme added to the beginning (prefix) or end (suffix) of a word to modify its meaning or grammatical function.

Allophone – A variant pronunciation of a phoneme that does not change the meaning of a word.
